What are natural resources? Name their two broad types.
questions.a: Materials from nature that satisfy our needs; they are inexhaustible (air, sunlight) and exhaustible (coal, petroleum, forests).

questions.q: Why are coal and petroleum called exhaustible?
questions.a: They formed over millions of years and cannot be remade quickly, so stocks run out with use.

questions.q: Classify water, sunlight and natural gas.
questions.a: Water and sunlight are inexhaustible; natural gas is exhaustible.

questions.q: How was coal formed in nature?
questions.a: Forests buried under earth millions of years ago were slowly compressed and heated, turning into coal (carbonisation).

questions.q: Why is coal called a fossil fuel?
questions.a: It formed from remains of ancient plants, like fossils, and burns to give energy.

questions.q: Name the variety of coal with the highest carbon content.
questions.a: Anthracite is the hardest coal with the most carbon; bituminous and lignite have less.

concepts.title: Products of Coal: Coke, Coal Tar, and Coal Gas

questions.q: Name the three useful products of coal.
questions.a: Coke, coal tar and coal gas.

questions.q: What is coke used for?
questions.a: Coke (a hard, porous, almost pure carbon) is used to reduce metal oxides in steel making and as a smokeless fuel.

questions.q: Which coal product gives naphthalene balls and synthetic dyes?
questions.a: Coal tar - a black liquid with many useful chemicals.

questions.q: How did petroleum form?
questions.a: Tiny plants and animals buried under the sea decayed for ages under heat and pressure, turning into petroleum trapped between rock layers.

questions.q: Why is petroleum called 'black gold'?
questions.a: It is as precious as gold - from it come fuel, plastics, synthetic fibres and many chemicals.

questions.q: Where does petroleum occur in the earth?
questions.a: It collects under impervious rock layers, often above natural gas, deep below the surface.

questions.q: What is petroleum refining?
questions.a: Separating crude petroleum into useful fractions by fractional distillation in a refinery.

questions.q: Name four fractions obtained from petroleum refining.
questions.a: Petroleum gas, petrol, kerosene and diesel (also lubricating oil, paraffin wax, asphalt).

questions.q: Which petroleum fraction is used as cooking fuel at home?
questions.a: Liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) from the top of the fractionating column.

questions.q: What are petrochemicals?
questions.a: Chemicals made from petroleum and natural gas, used to make plastics, synthetic fibres, dyes and detergents.

questions.q: Name two products made from petrochemicals.
questions.a: Polythene (plastic) and polyester cloth; also synthetic rubber and detergents.

questions.q: Why must we use fossil fuels carefully?
questions.a: They are exhaustible and burning them pollutes air; conserving them keeps them for future generations.

concepts.title: Natural Gas and Compressed Natural Gas (CNG)

questions.q: What is natural gas and why is it a clean fuel?
questions.a: A fossil fuel of mostly methane stored deep under earth; it burns with little smoke and residue.

questions.q: What is CNG? Where is it used?
questions.a: Compressed natural gas - natural gas squeezed at high pressure - used as a cleaner vehicle fuel in Delhi and other cities.

questions.q: Name the gas that fills balloons for weather study and parties.
questions.a: Helium, found along with natural gas deposits.

concepts.title: Conservation of Natural Resources and PCRA Guidelines

questions.q: What is PCRA and what does it advise?
questions.a: Petroleum Conservation Research Association - it advises driving smoothly, proper tyre pressure, regular engine checks and switching off engines at red lights to save fuel.

questions.q: List three habits that save fuel at home and on the road.
questions.a: Using public transport or car pools, keeping vehicle engines tuned, and cooking in pressure cookers or on low flame.

questions.q: Why should we switch to alternative energy sources?
questions.a: Fossil fuels are limited and polluting; solar, wind and hydel energy are renewable and cleaner.
